description: Hi everyone! I'm excited to connect with other participants, share ideas, and collaborate on an interesting project. I'm passionate about learning new things, solving problems, and developing creative solutions. I enjoy working with others, exploring new technologies, and challenging myself to build new skills.
summary:
We built Earth to Space, a web-based health monitoring prototype for astronauts on long deep-space missions. On the way to Mars, a message to doctors on Earth can take up to 22 minutes each way. A crew can’t wait for flight surgeons to interpret every reading, so our system gives astronauts the readings, what they mean and the next step, right on board.

The Analysis page compares vital signs like heart rate, blood pressure and blood oxygen against ranges adjusted for space. It flags each one green, yellow or red and highlights the affected body systems on interactive 3D anatomy models. A Daily Check-in tracks sleep, mood, symptoms, exercise and medication, and private entries stay with the astronaut. How It Works shows the signal path from suit sensors to the spacecraft computer, including live filtering of heart and brain signals. Our ranges and risks are grounded in NASA’s Human Research Program and its five hazards of spaceflight.

This matters because radiation, isolation, distance, altered gravity and closed environments slowly change the body, and small changes caught early can prevent emergencies. Earth to Space helps crews catch those changes themselves, without depending on Earth.
details:
• Vitals Analysis: Astronauts enter readings such as blood pressure, resting heart rate, blood oxygen, temperature and blood glucose. Each reading is compared against either Earth ranges or Space ranges adjusted for microgravity, then rated green, yellow or red. The system explains what the reading means, how spaceflight affects it, and which body parts are involved. Those parts are highlighted on two interactive 3D anatomy models (muscles, skeleton, organs and vessels) that can be rotated and zoomed separately.
  • Daily Check-in: A short form covers mood, stress, fatigue, sleep, symptoms, exercise, medication, a quick vision-grid test and a reaction-time test. Entries can be kept private on board or shared with the flight surgeon.
  • How It Works: An animated signal path follows data from suit sensors, through filtering and amplification, to a wearable hub, the spacecraft computer and Earth. A live demo shows raw heart (ECG) and brain (EEG) signals being cleaned by real digital filters. It is linked to the values entered on the Analysis page.
  • Research: The NASA sources behind our ranges and risks.
dataRefs: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
